CALIBRATION END DETECTOR: DESIGN SPEC (design stage only; nothing in the repo was edited) 0. DECISIONS THIS SPEC IMPLEMENTS - The default calibration PWM becomes 128. CAL_DEFAULT_PWM goes 80 -> 128, along with the Python mirror, the GUI dialog default and its text, SETUP.md and GLOSSARY.md text, and every "calibrate at PWM 80" hint (the NoFeedback hint prints CAL_DEFAULT_PWM, so it becomes "calibrate at PWM 128" with no code change). CAL_PWM_MIN and CAL_PWM_MAX stay at 40 and 150 (raising the floor to 110 is left as an owner decision, see risks). CAL_KNEE_NUDGE_MAX_PWM stays defined as CAL_DEFAULT_PWM, so the knee nudge now ramps to 128. Pinning it at 80 is rejected: today FRKL could not break free at 80 or at 100. - Each end is found from current plus motion, and the drive stops at once (sections 2-6). - The recorded ends become the T limits: inset 8 edges at limit-switch ends and 25 edges at the extended end (section 8). The EEPROM layout does not change. - Everything else stays as it is: one joint at a time, curl-first order, partner gates, yaws never driven, the knee nudge, the fixed 700-edge hall hip sweep, and the SENS gate. - The optional slower final approach is NOT built (section 10). 1. WHAT THE 'current' FIELD IS TODAY (firmware facts) - LinearActuator::updateSensors() computes avgIS = 0.9*avgIS + 0.1*analogRead(pinIS) (controlConfig.alphaIS = 0.10). It runs once per loop for all six actuators, also during calibration: ActuatorManager::updateAll calls updateSensors() before LegCalibration::update. - The telemetry 'current' field is (int)avgIS, printed by LinearActuator::printTelemetry. It is a truncated point sample of that EMA, taken when TELEMETRY_INTERVAL_MS = 50 has elapsed (arduino.ino loop). In endcur-111808.log the measured FRONT frame period is 51.5 ms (mean of 2510 frames), so the leader loop runs about every 3 ms and the EMA time constant is about 30 ms there. Follower loops are faster, so their avgIS is noisier. - ActuatorCurrentTracker (CurrentPresent/Absent) is unchanged. - Measured IS levels: - 0 with EN low. - "Driven, motor not conducting" (limit switch open): FL hip 7-8, FRHL 11, knees at their switch 7. 11-23 presses on the follower hips read 6-9. - Running: 9-17. - Pressing the knee's leg stop: 13-24. 2. DETECTOR INPUT AND SAMPLING (new pure class CalibrationEndDetector in src/actuator/calibration_end_detector.h) - Plant addition: `virtual uint16_t motorCurrentTenths(uint8_t joint) = 0;`. It returns round(10*avgIS), clamped to [0, 65535]. ActuatorManager::CalibrationPlant implements it. - Call update(nowMs, driveEdges, currentTenths, rampDone) every loop of an eligible drive, in every phase except Settle. - Each loop: sum += currentTenths (uint32) and n++ (uint16). - When (int32)(now - nextSampleMs) >= 0, close sample k: - e_k = driveEdges clamped to int16, where driveEdges = hallDriveEdges(sign_, hallCount(j) - startHall_). - i_k = (sum + n/2)/n, which is the boxcar mean of 10*avgIS over the 50 ms; if n == 0, use the current value. - Reset sum and n, then nextSampleMs += CAL_END_SAMPLE_MS (50). If it is still in the past, set nextSampleMs = now + 50 (resync after a long loop: never two samples in one call, never a burst). - k is the 0-based sample index from the drive start; sample k is taken about (k+1)*50 ms after the start. - Storage: a ring of CAL_END_RING = 24 samples holding int16 e and uint16 i. - v_k = e_k - e_(k-4), in edges per 200 ms (0 for k < 4). - Median means sorted[n/2] of n values (insertion sort; for even n this is the upper middle). - Forward progress: track eMax. A sample with e_k > eMax sets eMax = e_k and lastFwd = k; sample 0 only seeds eMax. A bounce backwards at a stop is not progress. still = k - lastFwd. - kRamp = the first sample index at which rampDone is true. rampDone = LegCalibration phase_ != Ramp, i.e. the ramp has reached the move PWM. At 128 the ramp is 26 steps of 5 PWM per 20 ms, so 520 ms. 3. WHICH DRIVES USE IT - Eligible: plant.hasQuadratureHall() && sensor(j) != Pot at beginDrive && stage != NudgeOut. - retract = (sign_ < 0). This covers the hip curl, the knee uncurl and the hip nudge return. The rod's end is the actuator's internal limit switch, so the SWITCH rule applies. - extend = (sign_ > 0). This covers the knee curl, the knee nudge return and the hip sweep. The end is the leg's mechanical stop, or an obstacle, so the STOP rule applies. - leaving = !curl_ (uncurl drives, which must break free of the curl end). - Proven-Pot joints, Rev 1/Rev 2 builds and NudgeOut drives keep today's code: Grace, then tumbling Windows, and nudgeDone bounds. 4. UNARMED DRIVES (no running phase yet, e.g. the curl press of an already-curled joint or a knee nudge return) - No current rule applies; this is a stall-only "Still" end. - Curl drive: Still when rampDone, k >= minStill/50, k >= 10, and e_k - e_(k-10) < CAL_HALL_STALL_MIN_EDGES (3). - minStill = CAL_END_STILL_MIN_DRIVE_MS (1000). - For a Return-stage drive, minStill = max(1000, nudgeDriveMs_), where nudgeDriveMs_ = the nudge's drive time recorded at its stopToSettle (capped at CAL_HIP_NUDGE_MAX_MS 2000). A blind joint's return therefore drives at least as long as its nudge did; this replaces the old CAL_START_GRACE_MS + CAL_STALL_WINDOW_MS >= CAL_HIP_NUDGE_MAX_MS guarantee. - Pressing at an end drops from about 2.8-3 s (ramp + 1.5 s + 1 s window) to about 1.0-1.05 s of drive. - Uncurl drive: Still when (k - kRamp)*50 >= CAL_START_GRACE_MS + CAL_STALL_WINDOW_MS (2500) and e_k - e_(k-20) < 3. This is today's break-free allowance, evaluated on a sliding window. - A Still end keeps today's finishMove semantics exactly: - Curl motion = at least CAL_HALL_CURL_EVIDENCE_EDGES drive edges; otherwise proven-home acceptance, nudge, NoMotion, etc. - Uncurl: at least 450 edges, else BarelyMoved. - Return-stage checks are unchanged. 5. LEARNING THE RUNNING BASELINES (arming) - From (k - kRamp)*50 >= CAL_END_LEARN_DELAY_MS (200): runStreak = (v_k >= CAL_END_RUN_MIN_EDGES (4, i.e. 20 edges/s)) ? runStreak+1 : 0. - Arm when runStreak >= CAL_END_ARM_SAMPLES (6, i.e. 300 ms) and e_k >= CAL_HALL_CURL_EVIDENCE_EDGES (12). Arming implies the joint is already Hall: checkHallEvidence classified it at 12 edges. - At arming: iRef = median(i_(k-5..k)), vRef = median(v_(k-5..k)), kArm = k. No end rule is evaluated on the arming sample. - After arming, every "normal running" sample (v_k >= 4 and 100*v_k >= CAL_END_NORMAL_SPEED_PCT (75)*vRef) updates the references: - iRef += clamp(i_k - iRef, -CAL_END_IREF_STEP (3), +3). This is a step-limited median tracker, 0.3 count per 50 ms. - vRef = max(vRef, v_k) (peak hold). - Slow phases (decelerations, crawls) therefore never pull the references. 6. END RULES (armed drives; in each sample the signature rule is checked first, then stuck) 6a. SWITCH (retract only) - When still first reaches CAL_END_SWITCH_STILL_SAMPLES (3), freeze per stop: - ref = median, and refMin = min, of i over samples [max(kArm-5, lastFwd-20) .. lastFwd-1]. That is the up to 20 samples (1 s) before the last forward-edge sample; that sample's own current may already be falling. - arrive = v_lastFwd. - fast = 100*arrive >= CAL_END_ARRIVE_FAST_PCT (50)*vRef. - A new forward edge un-freezes. - On every sample with still >= 3: worst = max(i_(k-2..k)). Fire SWITCH when: - fast: 100*worst <= CAL_END_SWITCH_FAST_PCT (88)*ref; - slow: 100*worst <= CAL_END_SWITCH_SLOW_PCT (70)*ref AND worst < refMin. - Why two thresholds: - Hips arrive at speed and their current falls only 20-40% (FL 10 -> 8 at 80/120, 13 -> 8 at 150; FR 14-17 -> 11). A 25% threshold misses FLHL at 120. "Count dead from speed" plus a 12% drop is specific. - Knees crawl into their switch with the current already raised and fall 43-50% (13-14 -> 7). - Crawl stalls without a switch dip only to 0.82-0.91 of their reference and never below their reference minimum. The extra below-minimum condition applies only to slow arrivals. 6b. STOP, the mechanical end (extend only) - med4 = median(i_(k-3..k)). - slow = 100*v_k <= CAL_END_STOP_SPEED_PCT (25)*vRef. - hot = 100*med4 >= CAL_END_STOP_CURRENT_PCT (125)*iRef. - stopStreak = (slow && hot) ? +1 : 0. Fire STOP at stopStreak >= CAL_END_STOP_HOLD_SAMPLES (3). Together with the 200 ms speed window this is about 0.2-0.3 s of evidence. 6c. STUCK (either direction) - Fire when k >= 20, e_k - e_(k-20) < CAL_HALL_STALL_MIN_EDGES (3), and still >= CAL_END_STUCK_STILL_MS/50 (8, i.e. 400 ms without forward progress). - The 400 ms stillness lets the FLKL knee crawl into its switch at 120 (forward edges at most about 0.3 s apart) without a false stuck. The FRKL crawl at 80 (edges 0.5-1 s apart) is still called stuck. - A stall with neither signature is never accepted as an end. - If the expected signature never comes, the drive goes STUCK. An obstacle on a hip curl (retract, current up) is STUCK, not an end. An obstacle on a knee curl looks like the leg stop, as today; a proven knee is still caught by the curl-end tolerance check. 7. LegCalibration INTEGRATION (leg_calibration.h) - New phase LegCalibrationMovePhase::Detect, used after the ramp for eligible drives. Ramp completion goes to NudgeOut ? Nudge : (detecting_ ? Detect : Grace). - New members: CalibrationEndDetector end_; CalibrationEnd endKind_ (None/Switch/Stop/Stuck/Still); bool detecting_; uint16_t nudgeDriveMs_. - beginDrive: set detecting_ per section 3, endKind_ = None, then end_.begin(now, sign_ < 0, !curl_, minStill). - update(): keep today's order (timeout, checkHallEvidence, nudgeDone, hall-hip-sweep target). Then, if detecting_ and the phase is Ramp or Detect: kind = end_.update(...); if kind != None, set endKind_ = kind and stopToSettle(). The sweep target at 700 edges still wins before the detector. - stopToSettle of a NudgeOut drive records nudgeDriveMs_ = now - moveStartMs_. - finishMove: - Classification and the repeat are unchanged; armed drives have at least 12 edges, so classifyAtRest never runs for them. - printEnd appends a token only for detector ends: - " by=switch cur=/" - " by=stop cur=/" - " by=stuck cur=/" Values are in tenths of an IS count. Still, sweep, nudge and pot END lines are unchanged. - Then: if endKind_ == Stuck, call fail(StuckMidStroke, driveEdges). fail() stops all, clears the hall home, warns if nudged out, and the pass stops before the partner joint moves. - Everything else is unchanged: - Switch and Stop ends imply curl motion (at least 12 edges). - Knee uncurl still needs at least CAL_HALL_MIN_STROKE_EDGES. - A hall hip sweep that stopped on a STOP signature before 700 edges is SweepShort ("obstacle?"); if it stopped STUCK, it is StuckMidStroke. - The proven-home tolerance, home-moved WARN, (4a) Return, (4b) stroke checks and (4c) are untouched. - New LegCalibrationFailure::StuckMidStroke. Its reason text is: " stuck mid-stroke after edges at PWM

: raise PWM or check load" It is at most 76 chars with a 4-char joint name and a 6-char n, so it is within CAL_ROBOT_REASON_MAX_CHARS 78, and the leader's echo "CAL ROBOT FAIL FRONT: ..." stays under 100. - Timeouts are unchanged: - CAL_MOVE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120 s still ends a joint that creeps forever. Update its comment: moves at 128 are faster. - CAL_SETTLE_MS = 300 and the follower silence watchdog are unchanged. - CAL_START_GRACE_MS is now used only by pot windows and by unarmed uncurls. - Partner gates: curledMask is set only by accept(), as today. A STUCK or failed move never marks a joint curled. 8. WHAT IS RECORDED, AND THE T LIMITS (no EEPROM change) - The recorded end is the settled position after CAL_SETTLE_MS, exactly as today: the home for curl ends (setHome at the settled count) and the staged uncurl end. - In the replays: - Switch ends are exact: the recorded count equals where motion stopped, in 10/10 moves. - Stop ends fire 0-5 edges shallower than where the compliant creep finally ended. - Saved limits keep today's form, so CalData v2 and isValidStoredJoint are unchanged and there is no version bump: hip [0, CAL_HIP_SWEEP_EDGES], knee [-S, 0]. - In the hall frame the minStop side is always the retracted end, which is an actuator limit switch (hip curl end, knee uncurl end). The maxStop side is the knee's compliant leg stop, or the hip sweep end. - LinearActuator::setTarget clamps hall targets to [minStop + ACTUATOR_ENC_SWITCH_INSET_EDGES (8), maxStop - ACTUATOR_ENC_STOP_INSET_EDGES (25)]. These two constants replace ACTUATOR_ENC_TARGET_INSET_EDGES (12). - Hip T range becomes [8, 675]; knee T range becomes [-S+8, -25]. - With the 12-edge error deadband, a knee stays 13-37 edges inside its stop. An overshoot at a switch end only opens the switch. - Pot T, the range guard (ACTUATOR_ENC_RANGE_MARGIN_EDGES) and the stall guard are unchanged. - static_assert CAL_HALL_MIN_STROKE_EDGES > SWITCH_INSET + STOP_INSET. 9. DEFAULT PWM 128 (all places) - calibration_constants.h: CAL_DEFAULT_PWM = 128. Rewrite the comments that cite PWM 80 as the default or break-free speed; keep the historical 11-23 measurements labelled as PWM 80. - krabby_mcu.py: CAL_DEFAULT_PWM = 128, plus the docstrings "C 128" and "None = firmware default 128". - gui/app.py: CALIBRATION_HELP becomes "Use the default speed (PWM 128): ends are found from motor current and motion; below about PWM 110 a joint may stall short of its end and the run stops it as stuck mid-stroke". The dialog default follows the mirror. - SETUP.md: - Command table: default 128. - Speed paragraph. - Knee nudge: "never faster than PWM 128". - NoFeedback row: "calibrate at PWM 128". - New FAIL row for stuck mid-stroke. - Replace "ends show only in the counts" with the 2026-11-24 end-current results. - T-step text: insets 8/25, and "calibration runs at PWM 128". - GLOSSARY.md: the CAL entry says ends are found from current and motion; new entries for Limit-switch end, Mechanical stop, Stuck mid-stroke. - arduino.ino and actuator_calibration_command.h already use the constant: no edit, and arduino.ino and telemetry.cpp stay byte-identical. 10. SLOW FINAL APPROACH: NOT BUILT. The design shows it does not help. - Switch ends are recorded exactly at full PWM: the count stops dead. - At the mechanical end, the signature weakens as PWM drops: current rise FR +80% at 150, +60% at 120, +11% at 80. The stop depth also moves with PWM (FL 15/3/-5 at 80/120/150), so a slow approach would shift the home and weaken the evidence, while the 25-edge inset already absorbs the compliance. - Detection at full PWM already takes 0.1-0.3 s. 11. BUDGET - RAM: about 140 B (ring 96 B + detector state about 40 B + LegCalibration about 4 B). The last gate log showed 3382 B free, so about 3240 B are expected. Re-measure REV 3 and REV 2; the floor is 3000. - Flash: about +2 KB. - No float in the detector except the plant's 10*avgIS. 12. REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION AND VALIDATION - The Python reference that the firmware must match sample-for-sample is C:\Users\nickm\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\78c86551260afdf9\720ce176-f876-4a62-9959-4e2b88a4d5da\scratchpad\ced-design\detector.py. - Parity goldens are in C:\Users\nickm\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\78c86551260afdf9\720ce176-f876-4a62-9959-4e2b88a4d5da\scratchpad\ced-design\goldens.json: 40 robot moves, 3557 samples (e, i10, rampDone), and the expected verdict with its k.
